data.bug_class: heap-buffer-overflow (unbounded strcpy into fixed-size caller-supplied output buffer)
data.rationale: The fuzz target libidn2_to_ascii_8z_fuzzer allocates out2 as a 64-byte heap buffer and repeatedly calls idn2_to_ascii_4i((uint32_t*)data, size/4, out2, flags) (fuzz/libidn2_to_ascii_8z_fuzzer.c). Per its contract, idn2_to_ascii_4i receives an output buffer sized for at most 63 chars plus NUL. However, idn2_to_ascii_4i (lib/lookup.c:580-627) converts the input to UTF-8, runs the full idn2_lookup_u8() conversion, and then unconditionally does strcpy(output, output_u8) at lookup.c:621. idn2_lookup_u8 only enforces IDN2_DOMAIN_MAX_LENGTH (255) internally, never the 63-char label limit of the _4i API. A non-ASCII label (e.g. many multi-byte CJK code points) passes lookup validation but punycode-encodes to an ASCII ACE string longer than 63 characters, so strcpy writes far past the 64-byte heap buffer -> ASAN heap-buffer-overflow. This is CVE-2019-12290: the missing length check before the strcpy in idn2_to_ascii_4i is the root cause; reachability is direct from the fuzz target's (size & 3) == 0 branch with size >= 4.
